name: BVHLoader + CMU mocap
notes: 2026-11-01: Three.js BVHLoader plays BVH motion capture through AnimationMixer.setTime(t). Proposed data source: CMU Graphics Lab Motion Capture Database (http://mocap.cs.cmu.edu/); data terms are separate from code and unverified.
2026-11-01: Captured from conversation; listed-in-prd is the schema's listed-only status. Licence, version and maintenance not yet assessed.
2026-11-01: Triage: assess. Concrete job: human figures and character motion, absent from the catalogue.

2026-11-15: Three.js dev package.json reports 0.187.0; no separate BVHLoader release is available in reviewed sources. CMU site describes its data as free for research projects only; rights for other uses remain unverified.
source: conversation 2026-11-01: character and figure tooling gap
summary: Three.js BVHLoader parses BVH skeleton animation into an AnimationClip for playback by AnimationMixer; the data and loader are separate choices, so BVHLoader adds motion import without supplying motion capture.
use_when: When a Three.js scene needs BVH motion clips
When AnimationMixer can sample a clip at a requested time
avoid_when: When you need authored or rigged humans: mpfb
When you need a VRM avatar: three-vrm
license: Three.js / BVHLoader: MIT. CMU motion data is stated free for research projects; other use terms unverified.

assessment.version_seen: Three.js dev package 0.187.0; BVHLoader has no separate version established
assessment.last_release: Not established for BVHLoader separately; Three.js releases independently
assessment.rationale: BVHLoader is a Three.js addon loader, not a standalone toolkit; Three.js package.json on dev reports 0.187.0 and its code is MIT. CMU says its motion data is free for research projects, so that dataset is not cleared here for general production. Keep the loader candidate for user-supplied/licensed BVH clips.
